newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukraine plans $350-$500 mln Sept Eurobond - Shpek.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine plans $350-$500 mln Sept Eurobond - Shpek.

text.p: The head of Ukraine's development agency said on Friday that the former Soviet republic planned to raise $350-$500 million in a Eurobond to be issued in September.
"In terms of the volume of bonds in the first tranche, we plan to raise $350-$500 million," Roman Shpek, head of Ukraine's National Agency for Reconstruction and Development, told a news conference.
Serhiy Tyhypko, Deputy Prime Minister in charge of reforms, said this week that Ukraine would launch a yen bond in Japan in September and a separate Eurobond that month or the next.

Shpek referred to a September issue for the Eurobond, which is to be lead managed by Deutsche Morgan Grenfell. He did not say what denomination the Eurobond would be in, though Deputy Finance Minister Mykhailo Honcharuk has said it would be in German marks or dollars.

Central bank chief Viktor Yushchenko has said Ukraine plans to raise $300 million to $900 million this year from foreign bond issues in part to finance the budget deficit which was finally agreed in parliament only on June 27.

Shpek said no rating agency had been chosen yet for Ukraine, and declined to forecast a rating, saying: "It's better to have a low rating than no rating at all". Tyhypko said in June Ukraine expected a rating similar to that of "our closest neighbours" -- Russia's rating with Standard & Poor's rating agency was BB- when it launched its debut Eurobond last year.
